latin: Peliaco quondam prognatae vertice pinus
english: Once, sprung from the Pelian peak, pines
note: pinus (plural) = the timbers of the ship Argo, built from pines of Mount Pelion.

latin: dicuntur liquidas Neptuni nasse per undas
english: are said to have swum through the clear waves of Neptune
note: nasse = navisse, 'to have swum'; liquidas: 'clear, liquid'.

latin: Phasidos ad fluctus et fines Aeeteos,
english: to the floods of Phasis and the Aeetean bounds,
note: Phasis: river of Colchis; Aeetean = of Aeetes, king of Colchis.

latin: cum lecti iuvenes, Argivae robora pubis,
english: when chosen youths, the oak-strengths of the Argive young manhood,
note: robora: 'oaks, hard oak-wood', i.e. the strongest, the flower of the youth.

latin: auratam optantes Colchis avertere pellem
english: desiring to turn away from the Colchians the gilded fleece,
note: Colchis: dative/ablative of the Colchians; avertere = carry off.

latin: ausi sunt vada salsa cita decurrere puppi,
english: dared to run down the salt shallows with swift stern,
note: vada: 'shallows, waters'; puppi: 'stern', i.e. the ship.

latin: caerula verrentes abiegnis aequora palmis.
english: sweeping the dark-blue levels with fir-wood palms.
note: aequora: 'level surfaces', i.e. the sea; palmis: 'palms (of the hand)', i.e. the oar-blades.

latin: diva quibus retinens in summis urbibus arces
english: The goddess for whom, keeping the citadels in the topmost cities,
note: diva = Minerva, guardian of citadels; quibus is plural (the youths).

latin: ipsa levi fecit volitantem flamine currum,
english: herself made the chariot flying with light breath,
note: currum: 'chariot', i.e. the ship; flamine: 'blast, breath' of wind.

latin: pinea coniungens inflexae texta carinae.
english: joining the pine weavings of the bent keel.
note: texta: 'things woven', the joined planks.

latin: illa rudem cursu prima imbuit Amphitriten.
english: She first imbued with voyaging untried Amphitrite.
note: illa = the ship; Amphitrite (Greek accusative Amphitriten) = the sea; rudem: 'raw, untried'.

latin: quae simul ac rostro ventosum proscidit aequor
english: Which, as soon as with its beak it ploughed the windy level
note: quae: feminine singular, the ship; proscidit: 'ploughed up'; aequor: 'level', i.e. the sea.

latin: tortaque remigio spumis incanduit unda,
english: and the wave, twisted by the oarage, grew white with foam,

latin: emersere freti candenti e gurgite vultus
english: there emerged from the shining eddy of the strait, as to their faces,
note: vultus: accusative of respect ('as to their faces') with emersere; some take it as subject, 'faces emerged'.

latin: aequoreae monstrum Nereides admirantes.
english: the sea Nereids, marvelling at the portent.
note: monstrum: 'portent, marvel', i.e. the first ship.

latin: illa, siqua alia, viderunt luce marinas
english: On that day, if on any other, saw the marine
note: luce: 'light', i.e. day; marinas agrees with nymphas (line 17).

latin: mortales oculis nudato corpore nymphas
english: mortals with their eyes, with body bared, nymphs

latin: nutricum tenus exstantes e gurgite cano.
english: standing out as far as the breasts from the white eddy.
note: nutricum tenus: 'as far as the nurses', i.e. the breasts (nutrix = nurse; by extension, breast).

latin: tum Thetidis Peleus incensus fertur amore,
english: Then Peleus is said to have been set on fire with love of Thetis,

latin: tum Thetis humanos non despexit hymenaeos,
english: then Thetis did not despise human marriage-songs,
note: hymenaeos: 'wedding-songs', i.e. marriage.

latin: tum Thetidi pater ipse iugandum Pelea sensit.
english: then the father himself perceived that Peleus was to be yoked to Thetis.
note: pater = Jupiter; iugandum: 'to be yoked', i.e. joined in marriage.

latin: o nimis optato saeclorum tempore nati
english: O you born in the too greatly longed-for time of the ages,

latin: heroes, salvete, deum genus, o bona matrum
english: heroes, hail, race of gods, O good of mothers
note: bona matrum goes with progenies (23b): 'O good offspring of mothers'.

latin: progenies, salvete iterum . . .
english: offspring, hail again . . .
note: Line 23b is preserved only in the Veronese scholia on Vergil; the rest of the line is lost and the dots are Merrill's gap marker, kept here.

latin: vos ego saepe meo, vos carmine compellabo,
english: you I often, you with my song shall I address,
note: meo goes with carmine: 'with my song'.

latin: teque adeo eximie taedis felicibus aucte
english: and you above all, exceedingly increased by fortunate torches,
note: taedis: 'pine torches', i.e. the wedding torches, the marriage; aucte: vocative, 'increased, enriched'.

latin: Thessaliae columen Peleu, cui Iuppiter ipse,
english: pillar of Thessaly, Peleus, to whom Jupiter himself,
note: columen: 'roof-ridge, pillar', i.e. mainstay.

latin: ipse suos divum genitor concessit amores.
english: himself the begetter of the gods, yielded his own loves.
note: Jupiter had himself loved Thetis.

latin: tene Thetis tenuit pulcherrirma Nereine?
english: Did Thetis hold you, the most beautiful daughter of Nereus?
note: Source misprint 'pulcherrirma' for pulcherrima, kept verbatim in latin. Nereine: 'daughter of Nereus'.

latin: tene suam Tethys concessit ducere neptem
english: Did Tethys grant you to lead home her own granddaughter
note: ducere: 'to lead', i.e. to take as wife.

latin: Oceanusque, mari totum qui amplectitur orbem?
english: and Oceanus, who embraces the whole globe with sea?

latin: quae simul optatae finito tempore luces
english: Which longed-for days, as soon as, the time being finished,
note: quae: feminine plural, referring to luces ('lights', i.e. days).

latin: advenere, domum conventu tota frequentat
english: arrived, the house with gathering all throngs
note: tota (with Thessalia, line 33) is the subject: all Thessaly throngs the house.

latin: Thessalia, oppletur laetanti regia coetu:
english: Thessaly, the palace is filled with a rejoicing company:

latin: dona ferunt prae se, declarant gaudia vultu.
english: they bear gifts before them, they declare joys with their face.

latin: deseritur Cieros, linquunt Phthiotica Tempe
english: Cieros is deserted, they leave Phthiotic Tempe
note: Cieros: town in Thessaly; Phthiotic: of Phthia.

latin: Crannonisque domos ac moenia Larisaea,
english: and the homes of Crannon and the Larisaean walls,

latin: Pharsalum coeunt, Pharsalia tecta frequentant.
english: they come together at Pharsalus, they throng the Pharsalian roofs.
note: tecta: 'roofs', i.e. houses.

latin: rura colit nemo, mollescunt colla iuvencis,
english: No one tills the fields, the necks grow soft for the bullocks,
note: The oxen are not yoked, so their necks lose the hardness of the yoke.

latin: non humilis curvis purgatur vinea rastris,
english: not is the low vine cleansed with curved rakes,

latin: non glaebam prono convellit vomere taurus,
english: not does the bull tear up the clod with down-sloping ploughshare,

latin: non falx attenuat frondatorum arboris umbram,
english: not does the sickle of the pruners thin the shade of the tree,

latin: squalida desertis robigo infertur aratris.
english: squalid rust is brought upon the deserted ploughs.

latin: ipsius at sedes, quacumque opulenta recessit
english: But his own abode, wherever the opulent receded
note: ipsius = of Peleus himself; recessit: 'withdrew', i.e. extended back into its inner rooms.

latin: regia, fulgenti splendent auro atque argento.
english: palace, gleams with shining gold and silver.
note: splendent is plural, agreeing with sedes.

latin: candet ebur soliis, conlucent pocula mensae,
english: Ivory gleams white on the thrones, cups shine together on the table,

latin: tota domus gaudet regali splendida gaza.
english: the whole house rejoices, splendid with royal treasure.

latin: pulvinar vero divae geniale locatur
english: The nuptial couch of the goddess, indeed, is placed
note: pulvinar: a cushioned couch (properly one for gods); geniale: of the marriage-bed.

latin: sedibus in mediis, Indo quod dente politum
english: in the middle of the abode, which, polished with Indian tooth,
note: dente: 'tooth', i.e. ivory; quod: neuter, the couch.

latin: tincta tegit roseo conchyli purpura fuco.
english: purple of the shellfish, dyed with rosy dye, covers.
note: conchyli purpura: the purple of the murex shell; the purple coverlet covers the couch.

latin: haec vestis priscis hominum variata figuris
english: This coverlet, varied with the ancient figures of men,
note: vestis: 'garment, cloth', here the embroidered coverlet.

latin: heroum mira virtutes indicat arte.
english: shows the virtues of heroes with wondrous art.

latin: namque fluentisono prospectans litore Diae
english: For, looking out from the wave-sounding shore of Dia,
note: Dia: the island (identified with Naxos) where Ariadna was left.

latin: Thesea cedentem celeri cum classe tuetur
english: she watches Theseus departing with swift fleet,

latin: indomitos in corde gerens Ariadna furores,
english: Ariadna, bearing untamed madnesses in her heart,
note: furores (plural): 'madnesses, frenzies'.

latin: necdum etiam sese quae visit visere credit,
english: and not yet even does she believe that she sees what she sees,

latin: ut pote fallaci quae tunc primum excita somno
english: inasmuch as she, then first roused from deceitful sleep,
note: ut pote ... quae: 'as being one who'.

latin: desertam in sola miseram se cernat harena.
english: sees herself, deserted, wretched, on the lonely sand.

latin: immemor at iuvenis fugiens pellit vada remis,
english: But the unmindful youth, fleeing, strikes the shallows with oars,
note: immemor: 'unmindful, forgetful'.

latin: irrita ventosae linquens promissa procellae.
english: leaving unfulfilled promises to the windy gale.

latin: quem procul ex alga maestis Minois ocellis
english: Him, far off, from the seaweed, with sad little eyes the daughter of Minos,
note: Minois: 'daughter of Minos' = Ariadna; alga: 'seaweed', i.e. the shore.

latin: saxea ut effigies bacchantis prospicit, eheu,
english: like a stone image of a bacchant, looks out at, alas,

latin: prospicit et magnis curarum fluctuat undis,
english: looks out at, and tosses on great waves of cares,

latin: non flavo retinens subtilem vertice mitram,
english: not keeping the fine headband on her yellow head,
note: mitram: the mitra, a headband or snood; vertice: 'crown, head'.

latin: non contecta levi velatum pectus amictu,
english: not covered, as to her veiled breast, with the light mantle,
note: pectus: accusative of respect; velatum (once veiled) is proleptic.

latin: non tereti strophio lactentis vincta papillas,
english: not bound, as to her milky breasts, with the smooth breast-band,
note: papillas: 'nipples, breasts'; strophio: a band worn round the breasts; tereti: 'rounded, smooth'.

latin: omnia quae toto delapsa e corpore passim
english: all which, slipped down from her whole body everywhere,

latin: ipsius ante pedes fluctus salis adludebant.
english: before her very feet the waves of the salt were playing upon.
note: salis: 'of salt', i.e. of the sea.

latin: sic neque tum mitrae neque tum fluitantis amictus
english: So neither then for the headband nor then for the floating mantle's
note: vicem (line 69) governs the genitives: 'the plight of the headband ... of the mantle'.

latin: illa vicem curans toto ex te pectore, Theseu,
english: plight she caring, on you, from her whole breast, Theseus,
note: ex te ... pendebat (line 70): 'hung on you'.

latin: toto animo, tota pendebat perdita mente.
english: with whole soul, with whole mind she was hanging, lost.
note: perdita: 'lost, ruined', i.e. desperately in love.

latin: ah misera, adsiduis quam luctibus exsternavit
english: Ah wretched girl, whom with unceasing griefs drove out of her mind
note: exsternavit: 'maddened, drove out of her senses'.

latin: spinosas Erycina serens in pectore curas
english: Erycina, sowing thorny cares in her breast,
note: Erycina = Venus of Eryx.

latin: illa tempestate, ferox quo ex tempore Theseus
english: at that season, from which time fierce Theseus,

latin: egressus curvis e litoribus Piraei
english: having gone out from the curved shores of Piraeus,

latin: attigit iniusti regis Gortynia tecta.
english: reached the Gortynian roofs of the unjust king.
note: Gortynian = Cretan (Gortyn, a Cretan city); the king is Minos.

latin: nam perhibent olim crudeli peste coactam
english: For they relate that once, compelled by a cruel plague
note: coactam: feminine singular, agreeing with Cecropiam (line 79), i.e. Athens.

latin: Androgeoneae poenas exsolvere caedis
english: to pay the penalties of the Androgeonean slaughter,
note: Androgeos, son of Minos, killed at Athens.

latin: electos iuvenes simul et decus innuptarum
english: chosen youths and at the same time the pride of the unmarried girls

latin: Cecropiam solitam esse dapem dare Minotauro.
english: Cecropia was accustomed to give as a feast to the Minotaur.
note: Cecropia = Athens (from Cecrops); dapem: 'feast, banquet'.

latin: quis angusta malis cum moenia vexarentur,
english: With which ills when the narrow walls were vexed,
note: quis = quibus, referring to these ills; angusta: 'narrow, straitened'.

latin: ipse suum Theseus pro caris corpus Athenis
english: Theseus himself, for dear Athens, his own body

latin: proicere optavit potius quam talia Cretam
english: chose to cast forth rather than that such to Crete

latin: funera Cecropiae nec funera portarentur.
english: funerals of Cecropia, and not funerals, should be carried.
note: funera: 'funerals, corpses'; funera nec funera: living victims, dead and yet not dead.

latin: atque ita nave levi nitens ac lenibus auris
english: And so, striving with light ship and gentle breezes,

latin: magnanimum ad Minoa venit sedesque superbas.
english: he comes to great-souled Minos and his proud seats.
note: Minoa: Greek accusative of Minos.

latin: hunc simul ac cupido conspexit lumine virgo
english: Him, as soon as with desiring light the maiden
note: lumine: 'light', i.e. eye.

latin: regia, quam suavis exspirans castus odores
english: royal looked on, whom, breathing out sweet scents, the chaste
note: conspexit (line 86) belongs to this sentence; virgo regia = the royal maiden, Ariadna.

latin: lectulus in molli complexu matris alebat,
english: little bed nourished in the soft embrace of her mother,

latin: quales Eurotae progignunt flumina myrtos
english: such as the streams of the Eurotas bring forth, myrtles,

latin: aurave distinctos educit verna colores,
english: or the spring breeze draws out, distinct colours,
note: distinctos colores: flowers of various colours.

latin: non prius ex illo flagrantia declinavit
english: not before from him did she turn away her burning

latin: lumina quam cuncto concepit corpore flammam
english: lights than she conceived flame in all her body
note: lumina: 'lights', i.e. eyes.

latin: funditus atque imis exarsit tota medullis.
english: from the depths and blazed up wholly in her inmost marrows.

latin: heu misere exagitans immiti corde furores,
english: Alas, wretchedly stirring up madnesses with unkind heart,
note: Addressed to Cupid; misere: 'wretchedly, cruelly'.

latin: sancte puer, curis hominum qui gaudia misces,
english: holy boy, who mingle joys with the cares of men,

latin: quaeque regis Golgos quaeque Idalium frondosum,
english: and you who rule Golgi and who leafy Idalium,
note: Venus; Golgi and Idalium are Cypriot cult-places.

latin: qualibus incensam iactastis mente puellam
english: on what, inflamed in mind, have you tossed the girl
note: qualibus agrees with fluctibus (line 98): 'on what waves'.

latin: fluctibus in flavo saepe hospite suspirantem!
english: waves, often sighing for the yellow-haired guest!
note: flavo hospite: the fair-haired stranger, Theseus.

latin: quantos illa tulit languenti corde timores,
english: How great fears she bore in her fainting heart,

latin: quanto saepe magis fulgore expalluit auri,
english: by how much more often she grew pale than the gleam of gold,
note: fulgore auri: ablative of comparison, 'paler than the gleam of gold'.

latin: cum saevum cupiens contra contendere monstrum
english: when, desiring to contend against the savage monster,

latin: aut mortem appeteret Theseus aut praemia laudis.
english: Theseus sought either death or the rewards of praise.

latin: non ingrata tamen frustra munuscula divis
english: Not unwelcome, yet in vain, little gifts to the gods
note: Her offerings pleased the gods, yet her vows (that he survive and stay) proved vain in the end.

latin: promittens tacito succendit vota labello.
english: promising, she kindled vows with silent little lip.
note: labello: diminutive of labrum, 'little lip'.

latin: nam velut in summo quatientem bracchia Tauro
english: For as, on topmost Taurus, shaking its arms,
note: Taurus: the mountain range; bracchia: 'arms', i.e. branches.

latin: quercum aut conigeram sudanti cortice pinum
english: an oak or a cone-bearing pine with sweating bark

latin: indomitus turbo contorquens flamine robur
english: an untamed whirlwind, twisting the trunk with its blast,
note: robur: 'oak-wood, trunk'.

latin: eruit (illa procul radicitus exturbata
english: uproots (that, far off, driven out by the roots,

latin: prona cadit, † lateque cum eius obvia frangens),
english: falls prone, † and widely, of it, the things in its way breaking),
note: Line corrupt, obelus kept. The transmitted 'lateque cum eius obvia frangens' does not scan or construe; the common emendation 'late quaevis cumque obvia frangens' gives 'widely breaking whatever meets it'.

latin: sic domito saevum prostravit corpore Theseus
english: so, its body tamed, Theseus laid low the savage one
note: saevum: the savage beast, the Minotaur.

latin: nequiquam vanis iactantem cornua ventis.
english: in vain tossing its horns at the empty winds.

latin: inde pedem sospes multa cum laude reflexit
english: Thence, safe, he turned back his foot with much praise,

latin: errabunda regens tenui vestigia filo,
english: guiding his wandering footsteps with slender thread,

latin: ne labyrintheis e flexibus egredientem
english: lest him, going out from the labyrinthine windings,

latin: tecti frustraretur inobservabilis error.
english: the unobservable wandering of the building should frustrate.
note: error: 'wandering', i.e. the maze; tecti: 'of the roof', i.e. the building.

latin: sed quid ego a primo digressus carmine plura
english: But why should I, having digressed from the first song, more

latin: commemorem, ut linquens genitoris filia vultum,
english: recount, how, leaving the face of her begetter, the daughter,

latin: ut consanguineae complexum, ut denique matris,
english: how the embrace of her kinswoman, how at last of her mother,
note: consanguineae: 'blood-relation', i.e. her sister.

latin: quae misera in gnata deperdita laetabatur,
english: who, wretched, utterly lost in her daughter, rejoiced,
note: deperdita: 'utterly lost', i.e. passionately devoted to her daughter.

latin: omnibus his Thesei dulcem praeoptarit amorem,
english: to all these preferred the sweet love of Theseus,

latin: aut ut vecta rati spumosa ad litora Diae
english: or how, carried by raft to the foamy shores of Dia,
note: rati: 'raft', i.e. ship.

latin: venerit, aut ut eam devinctam lumina somno
english: she came, or how her, bound as to her eyes in sleep,
note: lumina: 'lights', i.e. eyes; accusative of respect.

latin: liquerit immemori discedens pectore coniunx?
english: her consort left, departing with unmindful breast?
note: coniunx: 'consort, spouse'.

latin: saepe illam perhibent ardenti corde furentem
english: Often they relate that she, raving with burning heart,

latin: clarisonas imo fudisse ex pectore voces,
english: poured clear-sounding cries from the bottom of her breast,

latin: ac tum praeruptos tristem conscendere montes
english: and now, sad, climbed the steep mountains

latin: unde aciem in pelagi vastos protenderet aestus,
english: whence she might stretch her gaze over the vast tides of the open sea,
note: aciem: 'edge, keenness', i.e. the gaze.

latin: tum tremuli salis adversas procurrere in undas
english: now ran forward into the opposing waves of the quivering salt,

latin: mollia nudatae tollentem tegmina surae,
english: lifting the soft coverings of her bared calf,

latin: atque haec extremis maestam dixisse querelis,
english: and that she, sorrowful, said these things in last complaints,

latin: frigidulos udo singultus ore cientem:
english: stirring cold little sobs with wet mouth:
note: The quotation (Ariadna's lament) runs from line 132 to line 201.

latin: sicine me patriis avectam, perfide, ab aris,
english: Thus, me, carried away from my fatherland's altars, faithless one,
note: sicine: 'thus?', 'is it thus that ...'; patriis: 'ancestral, of my fatherland'.

latin: perfide, deserto liquisti in litore, Theseu?
english: faithless one, on a deserted shore have you left, Theseus?

latin: sicine discedens neglecto numine divum
english: Thus, departing, the divine will of the gods neglected,
note: numine: 'nod, divine will'.

latin: immernor ah devota domum periuria portas?
english: unmindful, ah, do you carry home accursed perjuries?
note: Source misprint 'immernor' for immemor, kept verbatim in latin. devota: 'accursed, devoted to the gods below'.

latin: nullane res potuit crudelis flectere mentis
english: Could no thing bend, of your cruel mind,

latin: consilium? tibi nulla fuit clementia praesto
english: the purpose? Was no mercy at hand for you,

latin: immite ut nostri vellet miserescere pectus?
english: that your ungentle breast might wish to pity us?
note: nostri: 'us', i.e. me.

latin: at non haec quondam blanda promissa dedisti
english: But not these promises once did you give, coaxing,
note: blanda agrees with promissa; voce (line 140) completes it: 'with coaxing voice' in sense.

latin: voce mihi, non haec miserae sperare iubebas,
english: with voice to me, not these things did you bid wretched me hope for,

latin: sed conubia laeta, sed optatos hymenaeos:
english: but happy marriage, but desired wedding-songs:
note: hymenaeos: 'wedding-songs', i.e. the wedding.

latin: quae cuncta aerii discerpunt irrita venti.
english: all which the airy winds tear apart, unfulfilled.

latin: nunc iam nulla viro iuranti femina credat,
english: Now henceforth let no woman believe a man swearing,

latin: nulla viri speret sermones esse fideles:
english: let none hope that the speeches of a man are faithful:

latin: quis dum aliquid cupiens animus praegestit apisci,
english: they, while the mind, desiring something, longs eagerly to obtain,
note: quis = quibus, 'for whom', i.e. men (plural).

latin: nil metuunt iurare, nihil promittere parcunt:
english: nothing do they fear to swear, nothing do they spare to promise:

latin: sed simul ac cupidae mentis satiata libido est,
english: but as soon as the lust of their desiring mind is sated,

latin: dicta nihil meminere, nihil periuria curant.
english: the words not at all do they remember, the perjuries not at all do they care for.
note: nihil: 'nothing, not at all'.

latin: certe ego te in medio versantem turbine leti
english: Surely I you, turning in the midst of the whirlwind of death,

latin: eripui et potius germanum amittere crevi
english: snatched out, and decided rather to lose my brother
note: germanum: the Minotaur, her half-brother (son of her mother Pasiphae).

latin: quam tibi fallaci supremo in tempore deessem:
english: than fail you, deceitful one, in the supreme moment:

latin: pro quo dilaceranda feris dabor alitibusque
english: for which I shall be given to be torn apart for beasts and birds

latin: praeda neque iniecta tumulabor mortua terra.
english: as prey, and not, earth cast on, shall I be entombed, dead.

latin: quaenam te genuit sola sub rupe leaena,
english: What lioness bore you under a lonely rock,

latin: quod mare conceptum spumantibus exspuit undis.
english: what sea, having conceived you, spat you out from foaming waves.
note: The source ends the line with a full stop; the sense continues as a question.

latin: quae Syrtis, quae Scylla rapax, quae vasta Charybdis,
english: what Syrtis, what grasping Scylla, what vast Charybdis,

latin: talia qui reddis pro dulci praemia vita?
english: you who return such rewards for sweet life?
note: dulci vita: her saving of his life.

latin: si tibi non cordi fuerant conubia nostra,
english: If our marriage had not been to your heart,
note: cordi esse: 'to be dear (to the heart)'.

latin: saeva quod horrebas prisci praecepta parentis,
english: because you shuddered at the harsh precepts of your old father,
note: prisci: 'old-fashioned, aged'.

latin: at tamen in vestras potuisti ducere sedes
english: yet you could have led into your seats

latin: quae tibi iucundo famularer serva labore
english: one who would wait on you as a slave-woman with pleasant labour,
note: quae: feminine singular, Ariadna herself.

latin: candida permulcens liquidis vestigia lymphis
english: soothing your white footsteps with liquid waters,
note: vestigia: 'footsteps', i.e. feet.

latin: purpureave tuum constemens veste cubile.
english: or spreading your bed with purple cloth.
note: Source misprint 'constemens' for consternens, kept verbatim in latin.

latin: sed quid ego ignaris nequiquam conqueror auris
english: But why do I, in vain, complain to unknowing breezes,
note: auris = auras/auris: 'breezes'.

latin: exsternata malo, quae nullis sensibus auctae
english: maddened by ill, which, endowed with no senses,
note: quae: feminine plural, the breezes.

latin: nec missas audire queunt nec reddere voces?
english: can neither hear sent words nor return them?
note: voces: 'voices, words'; reddere: 'give back, answer'.

latin: ille autem prope iam mediis versatur in undis,
english: He, however, is now nearly turning in the midst of the waves,

latin: nec quisquam adparet vacua mortalis in alga.
english: nor does any mortal appear on the empty seaweed.
note: alga: 'seaweed', i.e. the shore.

latin: sic nimis insultans extremo tempore saeva
english: Thus, too much exulting, at the last time, savage

latin: fors etiam nostris invidit questibus auris.
english: Fortune has even begrudged ears to our complaints.
note: auris here is 'ears' (from auris), not 'breezes' as in line 164.

latin: Iuppiter omnipotens, utinam ne tempore primo
english: Almighty Jupiter, would that not at the first time
note: utinam ne: 'would that not'.

latin: Gnosia Cecropiae tetigissent litora puppes,
english: the Cecropian sterns had touched the Gnosian shores,
note: Gnosian = Cretan (Cnossos); Cecropian = Athenian; puppes: 'sterns', i.e. ships.

latin: indomito nec dira ferens stipendia tauro
english: nor, bearing the dire tribute to the untamed bull,

latin: perfidus in Creta religasset navita funem,
english: the faithless sailor had tied his cable in Crete,

latin: nec malus hic celans dulci crudelia forma
english: nor this evil one, hiding cruel under sweet form
note: crudelia agrees with consilia (line 176).

latin: consilia in nostris requiesset sedibus hospes!
english: plans, had rested in our seats as a guest!

latin: nam quo me referam? quali spe perdita nitor?
english: For whither shall I take myself back? On what hope, lost, do I lean?

latin: Idaeosne petam montes? ah, gurgite lato
english: Shall I seek the Idaean mountains? Ah, with wide gulf
note: Idaean = of Ida in Crete.

latin: discernens ponti truculentum ubi dividit aequor?
english: separating, where the truculent level of the sea divides?
note: aequor is the subject: the savage sea divides (me from Crete), separating with its wide gulf.

latin: an patris auxilium sperem, quemne ipsa reliqui
english: Or shall I hope for the help of my father, whom I myself abandoned,
note: quemne: interrogative relative, 'whom?'.

latin: respersum iuvenem fraterna caede secuta?
english: following a youth spattered with brotherly slaughter?
note: fraterna caede: the killing of her brother, the Minotaur.

latin: coniugis an fido consoler memet amore,
english: Or shall I console myself with the faithful love of my husband,

latin: quine fugit lentos incurvans gurgite remos?
english: who flees bending the pliant oars in the gulf?
note: quine: 'who, then?' (ironic).

latin: praeterea nullo litus, sola insula, tecto,
english: Besides, the shore with no roof, the island lonely,
note: tecto: 'roof', i.e. dwelling.

latin: nec patet egressus pelagi cingentibus undis:
english: nor does a way out lie open, the waves of the sea surrounding:

latin: nulla fugae ratio, nulla spes: omnia muta,
english: no means of flight, no hope: all things mute,

latin: omnia sunt deserta, ostentant omnia letum.
english: all things are deserted, all things show death.

latin: non tamen ante mihi languescent lumina morte,
english: Yet not before will my lights grow faint in death,
note: lumina: 'lights', i.e. eyes.

latin: nec prius a fesso secedent corpore sensus
english: nor sooner will the senses withdraw from my weary body

latin: quam iustam a divis exposcam prodita multam
english: than I, betrayed, demand a just fine from the gods
note: multam: 'fine, penalty'.

latin: caelestumque fidem postrema comprecer hora.
english: and call on the faith of the heaven-dwellers in the last hour.

latin: quare, facta virum multantes vindice poena
english: Wherefore, punishing the deeds of men with avenging penalty,

latin: Eumenides, quibus anguino redimita capillo
english: Eumenides, for whom, wreathed with snaky hair,
note: quibus: dative of possession, 'whose'.

latin: frons exspirantis praeportat pectoris iras,
english: the brow carries before it the angers of the breast breathing out,
note: exspirantis pectoris: 'of the breast breathing out (its rage)'.

latin: huc huc adventate, meas audite querelas,
english: here, here come, hear my complaints,

latin: quas ego, vae miserae, extremis proferre medullis
english: which I, alas for wretched me, from my inmost marrows to bring forth
note: vae miserae: 'woe to wretched (me)'.

latin: cogor inops, ardens, amenti caeca furore.
english: am forced, helpless, burning, blind with mindless madness.

latin: quae quoniam verae nascuntur pectore ab imo,
english: Which, since they are born true from the bottom of the breast,
note: quae: feminine plural, the complaints.

latin: vos nolite pati nostrum vanescere luctum,
english: you, do not allow our grief to vanish,
note: nolite pati: imperative, 'be unwilling to allow', i.e. do not allow.

latin: sed quali solam Theseus me mente reliquit,
english: but with such a mind as Theseus left me alone,

latin: tali mente, deae, funestet seque suosque.
english: with such a mind, goddesses, let him bring death on himself and his own.
note: funestet: 'pollute with death'.

latin: has postquam maesto profudit pectore voces
english: These words, after she poured them out from her sad breast,
note: voces: 'voices, words'.

latin: supplicium saevis exposcens anxia factis,
english: anxious, demanding punishment for the savage deeds,

latin: adnuit invicto caelestum numine rector,
english: the ruler of the heaven-dwellers nodded with unconquered divine will,
note: numine: 'nod, divine will'; rector = Jupiter.

latin: quo nutu tellus atque horrida contremuerunt
english: at which nod the earth and the bristling

latin: aequora concussitque micantia sidera mundus.
english: seas trembled, and the heavens shook the glittering stars.
note: mundus: 'the world, the heavens'.

latin: ipse autem caeca mentem caligine Theseus
english: But Theseus himself, as to his mind with blind darkness

latin: consitus oblito dimisit pectore cuncta
english: sown over, let go from his forgetful breast all things
note: consitus: 'sown, planted over'; mentem: accusative of respect.

latin: quae mandata prius constanti mente tenebat,
english: which, commanded, he had held before with constant mind,

latin: dulcia nec maesto sustollens signa parenti
english: and, not raising the sweet signals for his sad father,
note: nec: 'and not'.

latin: sospitem Erechtheum se ostendit visere portum
english: showed himself safe to be seeing the Erechthean harbour.
note: Erechthean = Athenian; i.e. he failed to show by the signal that he was coming home safe.

latin: namque ferunt olim, classi cum moenia divae
english: For they say that once, when, with the fleet, the walls of the goddess
note: moenia divae: Athens, the city of Athena; classi: ablative, 'with the fleet'.

latin: linquentem gnatum ventis concrederet Aegeus,
english: his son leaving, Aegeus entrusted him to the winds,

latin: talia complexum iuveni mandata dedisse:
english: having embraced the youth, he gave such commands:
note: The quotation (Aegeus' speech) runs from line 215 to line 237.

latin: gnate mihi longe iucundior unice vita,
english: Son, to me far more delightful, only one, than life,
note: unice: vocative, 'only one'; vita: ablative of comparison.

latin: gnate, ego quem in dubios cogor dimittere casus
english: son, whom I am forced to send off into doubtful hazards,

latin: reddite in extrema nuper mihi fine senectae,
english: restored to me lately at the extreme end of old age,
note: reddite: vocative participle, addressed to the son.

latin: quandoquidem fortuna mea ac tua fervida virtus
english: since my fortune and your fervent valour

latin: eripit invito mihi te, cui languida nondum
english: snatch you from me unwilling, for whom not yet weary
note: cui = mihi: 'for me', whose eyes are not yet sated; eripit is singular in the Latin.

latin: lumina sunt gnati cara saturata figura,
english: lights are sated with the dear figure of my son,
note: lumina: 'lights', i.e. eyes.

latin: non ego te gaudens laetanti pectore mittam,
english: not I, rejoicing, will send you with glad breast,

latin: nec te ferre sinam fortunae signa secundae,
english: nor will I allow you to bear the signs of favourable fortune,

latin: sed primum multas expromam mente querelas
english: but first I will bring forth many complaints from my mind,

latin: canitiem terra atque infuso pulvere foedans,
english: defiling my white hair with earth and poured dust,
note: canitiem: 'whiteness', i.e. grey hair.

latin: inde infecta vago suspendam lintea malo,
english: then I will hang dyed canvases from the wandering mast,
note: lintea: 'linens', i.e. sails.

latin: nostros ut luctus nostraeque incendia mentis
english: so that our griefs and the burnings of our mind

latin: carbasus obscurata decet ferrugine Hibera.
english: the canvas, darkened with Iberian rust-colour, befits.
note: decet (Merrill's text): 'befits'; many editors read dicet, 'will declare'. ferrugine: 'rust-colour', a dark dye.

latin: quod tibi si sancti concesserit incola Itoni,
english: Which if to you the dweller of holy Itonus grants,
note: incola Itoni: Athena, worshipped at Itonus.

latin: quae nostrum genus ac sedes defendere Erechthei
english: she who our race and the seats of Erechtheus to defend

latin: adnuit, ut tauri respergas sanguine dextram,
english: has nodded assent, that you sprinkle your right hand with the bull's blood,
note: The bull = the Minotaur.

latin: tum vero facito ut memori tibi condita corde
english: then indeed see to it that, stored in your mindful heart,

latin: haec vigeant mandata, nec ulla oblitteret aetas,
english: these commands flourish, and that no age may blot them out,

latin: ut simul ac nostros invisent lumina collis,
english: that, as soon as the lights shall look upon our hills,
note: lumina: 'lights', i.e. your eyes.

latin: funestam antennae deponant undique vestem
english: the yards may set down the funereal garment everywhere
note: antennae: 'sail-yards'; vestem: 'garment', i.e. the dark sail.

latin: candidaque intorti sustollant vela rudentes,
english: and the twisted ropes may raise white sails,

latin: quam primum cernens ut laeta gaudia mente
english: that, discerning as soon as possible, glad joys with mind
note: laeta gaudia: neuter plural object of agnoscam (line 237).

latin: agnoscam, cum te reducem aetas prospera sistet.
english: I may recognize, when a prosperous time sets you down returned.
note: aetas: 'age, time'.

latin: haec mandata prius constanti mente tenentem
english: These commands, formerly with constant mind holding,
note: tenentem agrees with Thesea (line 239); haec mandata is the subject of liquere (line 240).

latin: Thesea ceu pulsae ventorum flamine nubes
english: Theseus, as clouds driven by the blast of the winds

latin: aerium nivei montis liquere cacumen.
english: the airy summit of a snowy mountain, left.
note: liquere: 'left'; serves both the commands (which left Theseus) and the simile (as clouds leave the peak).

latin: at pater, ut summa prospectum ex arce petebat
english: But the father, as he sought a view from the topmost citadel,

latin: anxia in adsiduos absumens lumina fletus,
english: anxious, consuming his lights in unceasing weepings,
note: lumina: 'lights', i.e. eyes.

latin: cum primum inflati conspexit lintea veli,
english: as soon as he saw the canvas of the swollen sail,

latin: praecipitem sese scopulorum e vertice iecit
english: threw himself headlong from the peak of the crags,

latin: amissum credens immiti Thesea fato.
english: believing Theseus lost by unkind fate.

latin: sic funesta domus ingressus tecta paterna
english: Thus, having entered the roofs of the house funereal through paternal
note: funesta: 'made funereal'; paterna goes with morte (line 247): 'by his father's death'.

latin: morte ferox Theseus, qualem Minoidi luctu
english: death, fierce Theseus, such as to the daughter of Minos grief
note: luctu: old dative (= luctui); qualem (luctum) ... talem: 'such grief as ... such'.

latin: obtulerat mente immemori, talem ipse recepit.
english: he had brought with unmindful mind, such he himself received.

latin: quae tum prospectans cedentem maesta carinam
english: Who then, looking out at the departing keel, sorrowful,
note: quae: feminine singular, Ariadna (in the picture on the coverlet).

latin: multiplices animo volvebat saucia curas.
english: wounded, was turning over many-fold cares in her mind.

latin: at parte ex alia florens volitabat Iacchus
english: But from the other part flourishing Iacchus was flying
note: Iacchus = Bacchus.

latin: cum thiaso satyrorum et Nysigenis silenis
english: with the thiasus of satyrs and the Nysa-born Sileni,
note: thiaso: the god's revel-band; Nysa: the mountain where Bacchus was nursed.

latin: te quaerens, Ariadna, tuoque incensus arnore.
english: seeking you, Ariadna, and set on fire with love of you.
note: Source misprint 'arnore' for amore, kept verbatim in latin. tuo amore: 'with your love', i.e. love of you.
Gap marker kept: Merrill marks a lacuna here; the feminine plural quae (line 254) has no antecedent in the surviving text (the maenads).

latin: quae tum alacres passim lymphata mente furebant
english: who then, eager, everywhere were raging with frenzied mind,
note: quae: feminine plural, the maenads named in the lost line(s); lymphata: 'frenzied (by the nymphs)'.

latin: euhoe bacchantes, euhoe capita inflectentes.
english: euhoe, doing bacchic rites, euhoe, bending their heads.
note: euhoe: the bacchic cry, kept as in the Latin; bacchantes: 'revelling as bacchants'.

latin: harum pars tecta quatiebant cuspide thyrsos,
english: Part of them were shaking thyrsi with covered point,
note: cuspide tecta: the spear-point of the thyrsus covered with ivy or vine leaves.

latin: pars e divulso iactabant membra iuvenco,
english: part were tossing limbs from a torn-apart bullock,

latin: pars sese tortis serpentibus incingebant,
english: part were girding themselves with twisted serpents,

latin: pars obscura cavis celebrabant orgia cistis,
english: part were thronging dark rites with hollow caskets,
note: orgia: the secret rites; cistis: the sacred chests holding the cult objects; celebrabant: 'thronged, celebrated'.

latin: orgia quae frustra cupiunt audire profani,
english: rites which in vain the uninitiated desire to hear,
note: profani: 'the profane', the uninitiated.

latin: plangebant aliae proceris tympana palmis
english: others were beating tambourines with outstretched palms
note: proceris: 'long, outstretched'.

latin: aut tereti tenuis tinnitus aere ciebant,
english: or were stirring thin tinklings from rounded bronze,
note: tereti aere: cymbals.

latin: multis raucisonos efflabant cornua bombos
english: for many, horns were blowing out hoarse-sounding boomings
note: multis: dative, 'for many'.

latin: barbaraque horribili stridebat tibia cantu.
english: and the barbarian pipe was shrilling with horrible song.

latin: talibus amplifice vestis decorata figuris
english: With such figures amply decorated, the coverlet
note: vestis: 'garment, cloth', the coverlet.

latin: pulvinar complexa suo velabat amictu.
english: embracing the couch was veiling it with its mantle.

latin: quae postquam cupide spectando Thessala pubes
english: Which after, by eagerly gazing, the Thessalian youth
note: quae: neuter plural, these pictures.

latin: expleta est, sanctis coepit decedere divis.
english: was filled, it began to withdraw for the holy gods.
note: pubes (singular) is the subject; decedere + dative: 'to make way for'.

latin: hic, qualis flatu placidum mare matutino
english: Here, as with morning breath the calm sea

latin: horrificans Zephyrus proclivas incitat undas
english: roughening, Zephyrus rouses into forward-leaning waves,
note: proclivas: 'sloping forward'.

latin: aurora exoriente vagi sub limina solis,
english: with Dawn rising, beneath the threshold of the wandering sun,
note: limina: 'threshold', i.e. the gate of the sun.

latin: quae tarde primum clementi flamine pulsae
english: which, at first slowly driven by mild breath,
note: quae: feminine plural, the waves.

latin: procedunt, leviterque sonant plangore cachinni,
english: go forward, and lightly sound with the splashing of laughter,
note: plangore cachinni: 'with the beating of laughter', the plashing of little waves.

latin: post vento crescente magis magis increbescunt
english: afterwards, the wind growing, more, more they increase

latin: purpureaque procul nantes ab luce refulgent,
english: and, swimming far off, gleam back from the purple light,

latin: sic tum vestibuli linquentes regia tecta
english: so then, leaving the royal roofs of the vestibule,

latin: ad se quisque vago passim pede discedebant.
english: each to his own with wandering foot everywhere they departed.
note: ad se: 'to their own (homes)'; quisque with plural verb.

latin: quorum post abitum princeps e vertice Peli
english: After whose going away, first, from the peak of Pelion
note: princeps: 'first, foremost'.

latin: advenit Chiron portans silvestria dona:
english: came Chiron bearing woodland gifts:

latin: nam quoscumque ferunt campi, quos Thessala magnis
english: for whatever the fields bear, whatever the Thessalian region on great
note: quoscumque, quos agree with flores (line 282).

latin: montibus ora creat, quos propter fluminis undas
english: mountains creates, whatever, near the waves of the river,

latin: aura parit flores tepidi fecunda Favoni,
english: flowers the fertile breeze of warm Favonius brings forth,
note: Favonius = the west wind.

latin: hos indistinctis plexos tulit ipse corollis,
english: these he himself brought, plaited in undistinguished garlands,
note: indistinctis: 'unsorted, mixed'.

latin: quo permulsa domus iucundo risit odore.
english: by which, soothed, the house laughed with pleasant scent.

latin: confestim Penios adest, viridantia Tempe,
english: At once Penios is present, green Tempe,
note: Penios: the river-god Peneus; Tempe is object of linquens (line 287).

latin: Tempe quae silvae cingunt super impendentes,
english: Tempe, which woods overhanging above surround,

latin: naiasin linquens Doris celebranda choreis,
english: leaving to the Naiads to be thronged with Doric dances,
note: naiasin: Greek dative plural. Text doubtful: Doris is read by Merrill as 'Doric'; other editors emend (e.g. Minosim, linquens doris ...). celebranda: 'to be thronged'.

latin: non vacuus: namque ille tulit radicitus altas
english: not empty: for he brought, by the roots, tall

latin: fagos ac recto proceras stipite laurus,
english: beeches and laurels lofty with straight stem,

latin: non sine nutanti platano lentaque sorore
english: not without the nodding plane-tree and the pliant sister
note: sorore: the sisters of Phaethon, changed into poplars.

latin: flammati Phaethontis et aeria cupressu.
english: of flame-struck Phaethon and the airy cypress.

latin: haec circum sedes late contexta locavit,
english: These around the abode, widely woven together, he placed,

latin: vestibulum ut molli velatum fronde vireret.
english: so that the vestibule, veiled with soft leafage, might be green.

latin: post hunc consequitur sollerti corde Prometheus
english: After him follows Prometheus of skilful heart,

latin: extenuata gerens veteris vestigia poenae
english: bearing the faded traces of his old punishment,

latin: quam quondam silici restrictus membra catena
english: which once, bound as to his limbs to the flint with chain,
note: membra: accusative of respect.

latin: persolvit pendens e verticibus praeruptis.
english: he paid in full, hanging from sheer peaks.

latin: inde pater divum sancta cum coniuge natisque
english: Then the father of the gods, with his holy consort and children,

latin: advenit, caelo te solum, Phoebe, relinquens
english: came, leaving you alone, Phoebus, in heaven,

latin: unigenamque simul cultricem montibus Idri:
english: and together your only-born sister, dweller of the mountains of Idrus:
note: unigenam: 'only-born, of the same birth', i.e. his twin sister Diana. Idri: text doubtful (an obscure mountain name; editors vary).

latin: Pelea nam tecum pariter soror adspernata est
english: for Peleus, together with you, your sister spurned,
note: Apollo and Diana are absent because they scorned Peleus.

latin: nec Thetidis taedas voluit celebrare iugalis.
english: and did not wish to celebrate the marriage torches of Thetis.

latin: qui postquam niveis flexerunt sedibus artus,
english: Who, after they bent their limbs on the snowy seats,

latin: large multiplici constructae sunt dape mensae,
english: abundantly, with manifold feast, the tables were built up,

latin: cum interea infirmo quatientes corpora motu
english: when meanwhile, shaking their bodies with infirm motion,

latin: veridicos Parcae coeperunt edere cantus.
english: the Parcae began to utter truth-telling songs.

latin: his corpus tremulum complectens undique vestis
english: For these, a garment embracing on all sides the trembling body,
note: his: dative, 'for these', i.e. their.

latin: candida purpurea talos incinxerat ora,
english: white, with purple border, had girded their ankles,
note: ora: 'border, hem'.

latin: at roseae niveo residebant vertice vittae,
english: but rosy fillets rested on the snowy crown,

latin: aeternumque manus carpebant rite laborem.
english: and their hands duly plucked the eternal labour.

latin: laeva colum molli lana retinebat amictum,
english: The left held the distaff clothed with soft wool,

latin: dextera tum leviter deducens fila supinis
english: the right, now lightly drawing down threads, with upturned

latin: formabat digitis, tum prono in pollice torquens
english: fingers shaped them, now, twisting on the down-turned thumb,

latin: libratum tereti versabat turbine fusum,
english: turned the spindle balanced with rounded whorl,
note: turbine: 'whirl, whorl' (the weight on the spindle).

latin: atque ita decerpens aequabat semper opus dens,
english: and so, plucking off, the tooth always levelled the work,

latin: laneaque aridulis haerebant morsa labellis
english: and woollen bits, bitten off, stuck to the dry little lips,

latin: quae prius in levi fuerant exstantia filo.
english: which before had been standing out on the smooth thread.

latin: ante pedes autem candentis mollia lanae
english: But before their feet, of shining wool the soft

latin: vellera virgati custodibant calathisci.
english: fleeces wicker little baskets were guarding.
note: custodibant: archaic form of custodiebant.

latin: haec tum clarisona vellentes vellera voce
english: These then, plucking the fleeces, with clear-sounding voice

latin: talia divino fuderunt carmine fata,
english: poured forth such fates in divine song,
note: The quotation (the Parcae's song) runs from line 323 to line 381.

latin: carmine perfidiae quod post nulla arguet aetas:
english: a song which no age afterwards will convict of faithlessness:

latin: o decus eximium magnis virtutibus augens,
english: O exceptional glory, increasing it with great virtues,
note: Addressed to Peleus.

latin: Emathiae tutamen opis, clarissime nato,
english: bulwark of the might of Emathia, most famous by your son,
note: Emathia: Macedonia/Thessaly; nato: ablative, 'through your son' (Achilles).

latin: accipe quod laeta tibi pandunt luce sorores,
english: receive what on a happy day the sisters reveal to you,
note: luce: 'light', i.e. day.

latin: veridicum oraclum. sed vos, quae fata secuntur,
english: a truth-telling oracle. But you, which the fates follow,
note: quae: neuter plural object, 'the threads which the fates follow' in sense; the relative is addressed to the spindles (fusi).

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: adveniet tibi iam portans optata maritis
english: There will come to you now, bearing things desired by husbands,

latin: Hesperus, adveniet fausto cum sidere coniunx,
english: Hesperus, there will come with auspicious star the wife,
note: Hesperus: the evening star, which brings the bride.

latin: quae tibi flexanimo mentem perfundat amore
english: who may flood your mind with soul-bending love

latin: languidulosque paret tecum coniungere somnos
english: and prepare to join languid little sleeps with you,

latin: levia substernens robusto bracchia collo.
english: laying her smooth arms under your sturdy neck.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: nulla domus tales unquam contexit amores,
english: No house ever covered such loves,
note: contexit: 'covered over, sheltered'.

latin: nullus amor tali coniunxit foedere amantes
english: no love joined lovers with such a compact

latin: qualis adest Thetidi, qualis concordia Peleo.
english: as the concord present for Thetis, as for Peleus.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: nascetur vobis expers terroris Achilles,
english: There will be born to you two, free of terror, Achilles,
note: vobis: plural, 'to you' (Peleus and Thetis).

latin: hostibus haud tergo, sed forti pectore notus,
english: known to enemies not by his back, but by his brave breast,

latin: qui persaepe vago victor certamine cursus
english: who very often, victor in the wandering contest of the race,

latin: flammea praevertet celeris vestigia cervae.
english: will outstrip the flaming footsteps of the swift hind.
note: flammea: 'flame-like', i.e. lightning-swift.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: non illi quisquam bello se conferet heros,
english: Not any hero will match himself with him in war,

latin: cum Phrygii Teucro manabunt sanguine campi
english: when the Phrygian plains will flow with Teucrian blood
note: Phrygian, Teucrian = Trojan.

latin: Troicaque obsidens longinquo moenia bello
english: and, besieging the Trojan walls in long war,

latin: periuri Pelopis vastabit tertius heres.
english: the third heir of perjured Pelops will lay them waste.
note: The third heir = Agamemnon (Pelops, Atreus, Agamemnon).

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: illius egregias virtutes claraque facta
english: His outstanding virtues and famous deeds

latin: saepe fatebuntur gnatorum in funere matres,
english: often mothers will confess at the funeral of their sons,

latin: cum incultum cano solvent a vertice crinem
english: when they loosen the unkempt hair from their white crown

latin: putridaque infirmis variabunt pectora palmis.
english: and mark their withered breasts with feeble palms.
note: putrida: 'withered, flabby'; variabunt: 'will make varied (with bruises)'.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: namque velut densas praecerpens messor aristas
english: For as, cropping the dense ears, the reaper

latin: sole sub ardenti flaventia demetit arva,
english: under the burning sun mows the yellowing fields,

latin: Troiugenum infesto prosternet corpora ferro.
english: he will lay low the bodies of the Trojan-born with hostile iron.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: testis erit magnis virtutibus unda Scamandri,
english: Witness to his great virtues will be the wave of Scamander,

latin: quae passim rapido diffunditur Hellesponto,
english: which everywhere is poured out into the swift Hellespont,

latin: cuius iter caesis angustans corporum acervis
english: whose course, narrowing it with heaps of slaughtered bodies,

latin: alta tepefaciet permixta flumina caede.
english: he will make warm the deep streams with mingled slaughter.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: denique testis erit morti quoque reddita praeda
english: Lastly, witness will be also the prey given back to death,
note: praeda: Polyxena, the share of Achilles' spoil given to him after death.

latin: cum teres excelso coacervatum aggere bustum
english: when the rounded tomb, heaped up with lofty mound,

latin: excipiet niveos percussae virginis artus.
english: will receive the snowy limbs of the struck maiden.
note: Polyxena, sacrificed at Achilles' tomb.

latin: Currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence. The source capitalises 'Currite' here; the English is unchanged.

latin: nam simul ac fessis dederit fors copiam Achivis
english: For as soon as fortune gives the weary Achaeans the means
note: fors: 'chance, fortune'; copiam: 'means, opportunity'.

latin: urbis Dardaniae Neptunia solvere vincla,
english: to loosen the Neptunian bonds of the Dardanian city,
note: Neptune built the walls of Troy.

latin: alta Polyxenia madefient caede sepulcra,
english: the lofty tombs will be wetted with Polyxenian slaughter,
note: sepulcra (plural) of the one tomb of Achilles.

latin: quae, velut ancipiti succumbens victima ferro,
english: which, like a victim succumbing to the two-edged iron,
note: quae: feminine singular, Polyxena (implied in Polyxenia).

latin: proiciet truncum submisso poplite corpus.
english: will cast forward, with knee bent under, her headless body.
note: truncum: 'maimed, lopped', commonly 'headless'.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: quare agite optatos animi coniungite amores.
english: Wherefore come, join the desired loves of the soul.

latin: accipiat coniunx felici foedere divam,
english: Let the husband receive the goddess in a happy compact,

latin: dedatur cupido iam dudum nupta marito.
english: let the bride be given to the desiring husband now long since.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: non illam nutrix orienti luce revisens
english: Her the nurse, revisiting at the rising light,

latin: hesterno collum poterit circumdare filo
english: will not be able to surround her neck with yesterday's thread
note: The thread measured the bride's neck; a thicker neck next morning was taken as a sign of consummation.

latin: (currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi),
english: (run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles),
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: anxia nec mater discordis maesta puellae
english: nor the anxious mother, sad at the discordant girl's

latin: secubitu caros mittet sperare nepotes.
english: sleeping apart, will give up hoping for dear grandchildren.
note: mittet sperare: 'will let go hoping'.

latin: currite ducentes subtegmina, currite, fusi.
english: run, drawing the weft-threads, run, spindles.
note: The Parcae's refrain; subtegmina = the weft (threads drawn out for weaving); addressed to the spindles. Rendered identically at every occurrence.

latin: talia praefantes quondam felicia Pelei
english: Foretelling such fortunate things once for Peleus,
note: felicia agrees with carmina (line 383).

latin: carmina divino cecinerunt pectore Parcae.
english: songs, with divine breast the Parcae sang.

latin: praesentes namque ante domos invisere castas
english: For in person, before, to visit the chaste homes
note: praesentes: 'present, in person'; ante: 'formerly'.

latin: heroum et sese mortali ostendere coetu
english: of heroes and to show themselves to a mortal gathering

latin: caelicolae nondum spreta pietate solebant.
english: the heaven-dwellers, piety not yet spurned, were accustomed.

latin: saepe pater divum templo in fulgente, revisens
english: Often the father of the gods, in his gleaming temple revisiting,

latin: annua cum festis venissent sacra diebus,
english: when the yearly rites had come with festal days,

latin: conspexit terra centum procumbere tauros.
english: looked on a hundred bulls falling forward on the earth.

latin: saepe vagus Liber Parnasi vertice summo
english: Often wandering Liber, on the topmost peak of Parnassus,
note: Liber = Bacchus.

latin: Thyiadas effusis euantis crinibus egit,
english: drove the Thyiads crying euhoe with streaming hair,
note: Thyiads: bacchants; euantis: 'crying euhoe'.

latin: cum Delphi tota certatim ex urbe ruentes
english: when the Delphians, rushing in rivalry from the whole city,

latin: acciperent laeti divum fumantibus aris.
english: received the god gladly with smoking altars.
note: divum: accusative singular, 'the god'.

latin: saepe in letifero belli certamine Mavors
english: Often in the deadly contest of war Mavors
note: Mavors = Mars.

latin: aut rapidi Tritonis era aut Rhamnusia virgo
english: or the mistress of swift Triton or the Rhamnusian maiden
note: era (= hera): 'mistress' of Triton, i.e. Athena Tritonia; Rhamnusian maiden = Nemesis.

latin: armatas hominum est praesens hortata catervas.
english: being present, encouraged armed bands of men.
note: est hortata: singular, agreeing with the nearest subject.

latin: sed postquam tellus scelere est imbuta nefando,
english: But after the earth was imbued with unspeakable crime,

latin: iustitiamque omnes cupida de mente fugarunt,
english: and all put justice to flight from their greedy mind,

latin: perfudere manus fraterno sanguine fratres,
english: brothers drenched their hands with brotherly blood,

latin: destitit exstinctos natus lugere parentes,
english: the son ceased to mourn his dead parents,

latin: optavit genitor primaevi funera nati
english: the father desired the funeral of his first-born son

latin: Liber ut innuptae poteretur flore novercae,
english: so that free he might possess the flower of an unwedded stepmother,
note: Liber here is the adjective 'free', capitalised at line-start in the source; text doubtful (some editors read liber ut innuptae as Merrill, others emend). The father wants his son dead so that he may marry the young woman unhindered.

latin: ignaro mater substernens se impia nato
english: the mother, laying herself under her unknowing son, impious,

latin: impia non verita est divos scelerare parentes,
english: impious, did not fear to defile the parent gods,
note: divos parentes: the gods of the family, the ancestral spirits.

latin: omnia fanda nefanda malo permixta furore
english: all things speakable, unspeakable, mingled with evil madness,
note: fanda nefanda: 'right and wrong'.

latin: iustificam nobis mentem avertere deorum.
english: turned away from us the justice-making mind of the gods.
note: avertere = averterunt.

latin: quare nec talis dignantur visere coetus
english: Wherefore they do not deign to visit such gatherings,

latin: nec se contingi patiuntur lumine claro.
english: nor do they allow themselves to be touched by clear light.
note: lumine claro: the light of day.
